MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

This neuron fires on a just-introduced named entity — typically a country/city proper noun (or a short stand-in subject like "they"/"W") — at the moment it is first mentioned and about to be paired with or contrasted against another name later in the sentence; it is suppressed on entity/kinship mentions that follow such a first mention (e.g. "father" before "mother", "Boston" before "Celtics").

This neuron gives weak positive responses to generic mid-sentence function/qualifier tokens ("have", "of", "very", "almost", digits/spaces in numeric expressions) in plain explanatory prose, and is strongly suppressed (large negative) across tokens inside academic research-findings sentences ("the analysis revealed that... are the most critical parameters", "were found to be most stably expressed"), so it mainly discriminates ordinary informational prose from formal results-reporting language.
